criteria.evidence: Classical resolution before coherent entry preserves the existing fixed-shape machine. However, §§3.3 and 4.7 supply qreg operands at CC/R calls, not the region descriptors presumed by the new extent bindings.
criteria.change: In §5.1 state: "Every extent parameter is supplied through an explicit classical call-shape binding and validated against the actual register before any effect."

criteria.evidence: Literal substitution preserves existing instruction semantics. The proposed source rules explicitly cover wire[n] and loop/allocation bounds but do not enumerate parameter occurrences in reg widths, region types or width-bearing opcode suffixes.
criteria.change: In §16.2 state: "The permitted parameter occurrences are explicitly listed size positions; all other integer positions remain literal, and substitution precedes ordinary operand validation." Publish that list with the grammar.

criteria.evidence: Fixing widths classically and applying the existing invariants after substitution introduces no quantum-dependent sizing. Both XOR examples are correct; exhaustive arithmetic checks passed for all 64 n=1 tuples and 1024 n=3 tuples.
criteria.change: Optional clarification in §5.1: "A resolved family's denotation is exactly that of its literal substitution; control and adjoint preserve that same width binding."

criteria.evidence: Instance-sensitive cache keys and resolved integer catalog descriptors are appropriate. The existing scheduler and §10.1 estimator requests lack a separate width vector, while the proposal correctly forbids putting widths silently into ordinary args.
criteria.change: In §§10.1 and 11 state: "A standalone family scheduling or estimation request supplies the complete ordered width_args vector; its instance_hash is recomputed and validated before expansion."

criteria.evidence: Family versus instance identity is a sound distinction, but extent binding lacks an input channel and the closure-keyed certificate schema cannot represent different concrete frames for multiple instances of one family.
criteria.change: Extend §§9.4 and 12.3 with the instance-keyed certificate rule in LPE-2, including resolved signatures, frames and claim subjects.

criteria.evidence: The verification script passes and accurately checks the hand XOR values, without claiming consumer execution. The proposed conformance cases are useful but omit a single root containing two different widths of the same family.
criteria.change: Add to conformance: "One root invokes xor_width at n=1 and n=3 with empty ordinary args; both instances must coexist in its certificate with interface widths [1,1,4] and [3,3,4]."

criteria.evidence: The cited ISA and dialect premises check out, including dialect §8.4, §24 D34 and §25.3 G-17. The note correctly distinguishes existing denotational expressiveness from practical emission and preserves the full valid domain.
criteria.change: In the dialect append replace "classical but not statically finite" with "classical but not statically enumerated"; unsigned-i64 shape domains are finite.

criteria.evidence: The proposal gives a useful compact design and a responsible 0.10 release boundary. The advertised exact diff still leaves two normative contract decisions unresolved.
criteria.change: In the instantiation paragraph state: "Resolve explicit call-shape inputs, derive instance identity, substitute source sizes, validate the concrete region, and only then construct executable, schedule and certificate records."

blocking.section: Recommended exact spec diff: extent bindings; ISA §§3.3, 4.7, 5.1 and 16.2
blocking.problem: The diff reads extent parameters from "the caller's resolved region descriptor", but CC/R region calls have no such descriptor. Sections 3.3 and 4.7 pass a qreg and validate its total width against an already known region[A,W]; the ledger contains width, not A and W. Thus the presumed descriptor is not an existing call input. An eight-wire actual can represent region[1,4] or region[2,2]. Those shapes differ operationally: XORing integer 1 into cell 1 of an initially zero register produces flattened value 16 or 4 respectively. The proposed bind metadata identifies which axes to read but supplies neither axis at this boundary. Adding width_args to downstream bindings does not define how this source call supplies them.
blocking.fix: Extend §§4.7, 5.1 and 16.2 with an explicit classical call-shape vector, which I recommend: "Each CC/R family call supplies width_args in header parameter order, separately from ordinary args. A wire-bound entry MUST equal the actual operand's ledger width. Memory-axis entries supply A and W; after substitution, every memory actual MUST have exactly 2^A·W wires and satisfy the existing role and disjointness rules. All values are fixed before coherent entry; a mismatch raises FAULT_UB_TRAP before any effect. Nested coherent calls forward shapes from resolved caller declarations." Alternatively introduce typed region(q,A,W) actuals and read the axes from those; that also works but adds a new operand form. The eight-wire example must distinguish width_args ["1","4"] from ["2","2"], yielding 16 versus 4 for the cell-1 operation. Scheduling and estimation requests without register operands must supply the corresponding complete vector explicitly.

blocking.section: Recommended exact spec diff: instance bindings; ISA §§9.4, 12.1–12.3
blocking.problem: Adding width_args and instance_hash to certificate bindings does not repair the existing certificate record keys. Section 12.3 still permits one regions[closure_hash] record containing one signature and mandatory frame; §9.4 requires literal interface widths after instantiation and permits only c as a frame-expression variable. A fixed root action can invoke the same xor_width family at n=1 and n=3. Both children have the same family closure hash, but their slot widths must respectively be [1,1,4] and [3,3,4]. One existing record cannot satisfy both. The diff neither provides multiple instance records nor defines how claim subjects and inverse-pair references select them. This prevents a conforming certificate for the composed program, despite each instance being individually valid.
blocking.fix: Extend §§9.4 and 12.1–12.3, not only the root bindings. Recommended rule: "A concrete width-family certificate region record is keyed by instance_hash and carries closure_hash and width_args. Its signature, bounds, frame and domains are resolved for that instance. Claim subjects, inverse-pair references and composition references distinguish instances; verification for one instance MUST NOT discharge another. A parameter-uniform structural claim may cover multiple widths only by explicitly quantifying them and checking its side conditions throughout that domain." Alternatively retain the family closure key and nest records under instances[instance_hash]; either layout works, but choose one normatively. The mixed-width root must contain two child records with widths [1,1,4] and [3,3,4], and an n=1 claim must not certify n=3.

suggestions: Identity, §9.2: state "The instance-hash preimage uses the family's 64 lowercase ASCII hexadecimal closure-hash characters, followed by LF; width_args is the header-ordered JCS array of canonical unsigned decimal strings, followed by LF." Publish a byte-exact vector so consumers cannot choose raw digest bytes instead.

Grammar, §16.2: state "Substitution is capture-free and applies only to declared size positions; parameter names are resolved in a separate width namespace." Include reg widths, region axes and any supported width-bearing opcode suffixes explicitly; unsupported expression forms remain outside this extension.

Release and hashes: state "This proposal changes the 0.10 contract only. Every symbol re-emitted with isa=0.10 is rehashed under §9.2, including symbols without width parameters; published 0.9 objects and ref@0.9 remain unchanged." Publish the affected launch/sched/cert version selections and the 0.10 expansion-library default together. The current 219-recipe catalog check reproduces hash 5de4e4995350313e50217880ba1b95de39cd043283b726337d4894efb005d197.

Conformance: add "A false width_args/instance_hash pair rejects before replay; two different qreg ids with identical shape share instance identity; a single root may contain different instances of the same family." Preserve the existing n=1 result (1,1,0), n=3 result (5,6,0), and K79 address-only () rule.
path_to_accept: First define the classical extent-binding channel and its pre-effect checks (LPE-1). Then define instance-specific certificate records and references, including a mixed-width root example (LPE-2). With those changes I would accept the proposed 0.10 extension; the note expressly proposes no normative 0.9 K repair.
summary: The expressiveness diagnosis, XOR witnesses and frozen-0.9 catalog claims are correct. Classical width specialization preserves the accepted core semantics. Two contract blockers remain: CC/R extent descriptors are presumed but unavailable, and certificates cannot represent multiple shapes under one family closure key.
